question: A month with \(31\) days has the same number of Mondays and Wednesdays. How many of the seven days of the week could be the first day of this month?
solution:
Since \(31=4\cdot7+3\), the month contains four complete weeks plus three extra days. Every weekday occurs four times, and the three consecutive weekdays beginning with the month's first day occur a fifth time.

Monday and Wednesday have equal counts exactly when both are among those three extra weekdays or neither is.

If both are included, the three extra weekdays must be Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday. This gives one possible first day: Monday.

If neither is included, the block of three must avoid Monday and Wednesday. Tuesday is isolated between those excluded days, so the block must lie within Thursday through Sunday. The possibilities are Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Friday, Saturday, Sunday. These give two more first days: Thursday and Friday.

The two cases are disjoint and cover every way the counts can agree. Thus there are \(1+2=\boxed{3}\) possible first days, choice \(\text{B}\).
